audit.whatIsWrong: The lane was described in generic burst-mage terms with no mechanism named.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs reaches 1000 and grows larger, faster and longer-rooting after it passes through a champion or kills a unit — through a wave it is a much worse skillshot to dodge than in open ground.
audit.corrected: Even at 5.5/10; the difficulty is a 1000-range root that upgrades itself off the minions you are standing behind.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2..5].side all read 'Skill' while the content layer read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Kassadin, and win[4] said Neeko while whys[4] said level 6 flips to Kassadin.
audit.why: Riftwalk at 6 is the documented flip and the win rate supports the late rows.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Kassadin, Kassadin, Kassadin in both layers; win[4] moved with phases[4].side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said that Neeko has three separate ways to cancel Null Sphere, or that Pop Blossom's wind-up is invisible while she is disguised.
audit.why: Null Sphere is a channel; Tangle-Barbs roots, Pop Blossom knocks up and stuns, and Inherent Glamour's immobilising break condition means her CC lands from a body you read as an ally. Riot's text states the prep is hidden while disguised.
audit.corrected: Do not start Null Sphere while Tangle-Barbs is up — the root cancels it. And an ally-looking champion walking into you at 600 range is Pop Blossom's hidden wind-up.

audit.why: Tangle-Barbs is 12s down to 10s, Pop Blossom 120/105/90s, Blooming Burst 9 down to 7s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wave advice recommended standing behind minions against the root without noting the cost.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs becomes larger, faster and longer-rooting when it kills a unit, so a low-health wave is the worst thing to hide behind.
audit.corrected: Sidestep laterally rather than hiding behind a dying wave.

audit.why: 55.56% across 531 games matches an even-then-scaling verdict.
